Controller deviation B (portability): POSIX sh wrapper, milliseconds via Perl Time::HiRes, same-shell times, sysctl vm.loadavg else /proc/loadavg and sysctl hw.ncpu else getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN. sh -n and installed dash -n pass. Controller deviation C (speed): sampler interval 30 is asserted via header and a fixture sleep stub recording its argument, without waiting 30s or adding a production cadence knob. Fixture sleeps are at most 1s. Full 40-execution control measured 17.07s, below 60s.

Supplemental cleanup mutation removes both sampler kill and wait to avoid a deliberately unbounded wait; the case reaps the leaked fixture sampler.

Controller re-run outside the sandbox (iteration 56): the first AC1 run gave 40 cases, 1 failure (load-sampler on gmake); 5 reruns were green. Under 16 busy loops, 1 of 25 to 40 runs failed. Debug capture (set -x plus a copy of the fixture dir): load.tsv held a half row '<epoch><TAB>' because the sampler was killed during $(load1) and printf still wrote. That is a production defect (report would refuse the run), so the controller fixed it in tools/suite_profile.sh: write a row only when load1 returned a value. Also hardened the fixture: its recipe waits at most 5 s for the sampler's first sleep. After the fix: 0 of 80 under the same load; AC1 3/3 green (40 cases, 0 failures); AC4 9 cases, 0 failures; drills R and C killed; cadence-60 mutant still killed (rc 1). passes stays false until rig/full and the evaluator.

ROUND 2 executor evidence at base HEAD 6bf988fb (mission/stapledon-iter56-l4): read round-1 evaluator /tmp/stap56/eval_R1-RIG-TEST-SPEED_M1a_round_1.json (66/100 FAIL). Changed only tools/suite_profile.sh, tools/test_suite_profile.sh and these M1a notes. No git writes, Python, real suite target, held-file, Makefile, mk/* or rig_check.sh edits. All fixtures, mutations, logs and PID records stayed in mktemp directories; external guards remained observations. All passes/status/blockers remain unchanged; M1a passes stays false.

B1 fixed: overhead-200 still requires exactly 200 TSV rows. In the case's own shell, times is redirected before run and immediately after run (never via command substitution); the delta of line-2 child user+system CPU must be <=30000 ms. Wall must be <=200000 ms. Each make execution prints 'overhead-200: wall <ms> ms, cpu <ms> ms over 200 lines (<per-line> ms/line wall, <per-line> ms/line cpu)' in the case log and control output.

Deliberate design deviation: the design/plan's <=50 ms/line wall gate is now informational. Supplemental overhead mutation is now ~200 ms of busy CPU per wrapper invocation: perl -e '$s=(times)[0]+(times)[1]; do { @t=times } while $t[0]+$t[1]-$s<0.20'. It failed overhead-200 on both makes at 45582/45445 ms child CPU and 46662/46355 ms wall. Pure sleep overhead is caught only by the wall hang guard at roughly >=1 s per line; smaller pure waits deliberately do not fail the CPU gate. That 200-second sleep experiment was not run.

CPU fixture refinement: cpu-busy-sleep uses a fixed >=0.25 s child CPU workload and asserts >=0.20 s, replacing its load-sensitive CPU/wall >=0.5 ratio. The sleep <=0.1 s assertion remains. A syscall-heavy Perl recipe writes only its fixture syscall.data until its own system CPU reaches >=0.20 s, records its own user+system CPU in syscall.cpu, and asserts wrapper CPU >=that total minus 0.04 s. A sys-recipe-only user-time mutant independently proves this new assertion is reached and kills loss of system accounting.

Report fixtures: report-version now asserts failed-rc and closure-mismatch refusal messages. report-medians refuses absent -j8 plus invalid before=6 and after=1 or 7 jobs. report-load uses four serial inputs and an exact duplicate slot/attempt, so the duplicate-refusal diagnostic is tested while three distinct slots would remain if the guard were removed; the existing ordered retry/count assertion is retained.

Sampler fixtures: production sampler writes its in-flight sleeper PID to out/sleeper.pid. sampler-cleanup synchronizes on that file and asserts sampler and sleeper PIDs are gone after normal, TERM and INT returns; fixture cleanup kills either leaked process after a mutant. load-sampler tests empty successful sysctl output and empty fallback output, requiring no row at all and explicitly rejecting half rows. Since macOS lacks /proc, only the literal /proc/loadavg path is redirected to an empty readable fixture file in a scratch copy; load1 and the row guard remain verbatim. No production timing or load probe knob was added.
